name: keklick-copilot
description: Flexible custom model endpoints for GitHub Copilot Chat with multi-source API routing

baseUrl.title: Base URL
baseUrl.description: The endpoint URL for this provider (e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1).

commands.title: Open Agent Worktree in New Window
Apply Agent Worktree Changes to Workspace

customcopilot.logLevel.description: Debug log level. Logs are written to ~/.copilot/customcopilot/logs/ as JSON lines. Default is 'off' (no logging).

enumDescriptions: Scan skills before install/save; critical/high findings block, others ask for confirmation.
Scan skills but never block — every finding only asks for confirmation.
Do not scan skills at all (not recommended).
customcopilot.skills.safetyScan.description: Security scan for skills (exfiltration, prompt injection, destructive commands) applied to every file of a skill before it is installed or saved — from the Skills screen and from Copilot's skill tools.

customcopilot.logMessageContent.description: Privacy opt-in: when enabled AND logLevel is 'debug', full chat message content is written to the log file. Keep disabled unless you explicitly want conversation content (potentially including your code) persisted to disk.

customcopilot.proxyUrl.description: Optional global proxy URL for API requests (supports socks5://, socks5h://, http://, https://).

customcopilot.debugRequestLogging.description: When enabled, failed API requests are printed to the console (Help > Toggle Developer Tools) as a reproducible curl command plus the server response body. Sensitive headers (API keys, tokens) are masked. Useful for debugging request/response issues.

customcopilot.promptOverride.enabled.description: Override the system prompt that Copilot Chat sends for ALL models served by this extension. When enabled, the system prompt is rewritten (per the settings below) before being forwarded to your endpoint. Lets you replace or extend the default prompt and its parts (e.g. safety rules) with your own.

enumDescriptions: Do not change the system text with your text (find/replace rules still run).
Keep Copilot's system prompt and add your text after it.
Add your text before Copilot's system prompt.
Discard Copilot's system prompt entirely and use only your text.
customcopilot.promptOverride.mode.description: How 'customcopilot.promptOverride.text' is combined with the system prompt Copilot assembled. Only applies when 'customcopilot.promptOverride.enabled' is true.

customcopilot.promptOverride.text.description: Your custom system prompt text. Combined with the original system prompt per 'customcopilot.promptOverride.mode'. Use this to add stricter rules, change the assistant's identity, or fully replace the default prompt.

customcopilot.promptOverride.replacement.description: Surgical find/replace rules applied to the (combined) system prompt. Use these to rewrite individual PARTS of the default prompt — e.g. swap Copilot's safety block for your own stricter rules. Applied in order, after the mode/text combination.

find.description: Text (or regular expression, if 'isRegex' is true) to search for in the system prompt.

replace.description: Replacement text. Leave empty to delete the matched text.

flags.description: Regular expression flags (default 'g'). Only used when 'isRegex' is true.

displayName.description: (Optional) Display name for the model that will be shown in the Copilot interface. If not provided, will be generated automatically.

configId.description: (Optional) Configuration ID for this model. Allows defining the same model with different settings (e.g. 'glm-4.6::thinking', 'glm-4.6::no-thinking').

family.description: Model family (e.g., 'gpt-4', 'claude-3', 'gemini'). Enables model-specific optimizations and behaviors. Defaults to 'oai-compatible' if not specified.

baseUrl.description: Base URL for the model provider (required per model, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1).

proxyUrl.description: Optional proxy URL for this source (supports socks5://, socks5h://, http://, https://).

userAgent.description: Optional User-Agent override for this source. If omitted, global customcopilot.userAgent is used.

context_length.description: Model support context length. Default is 128000.

vision.description: Model support vision. Default is false.

tool_calling.description: Whether the model supports tool/function calling. When omitted it is inferred from the endpoint metadata or model id.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate (range: [1, context_length)). Default is 4096.

max_completion_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate (OpenAI new standard parameter).

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort level (OpenAI reasoning configuration). Clamped to the nearest weaker level the model supports; "none" disables thinking where supported.

thinking.description: Thinking configuration for Anthropic / Z.AI providers

type.description: Set to "enabled" to enable thinking, "disabled" to disable thinking, or "adaptive" to let the model decide (Anthropic adaptive thinking).

enable_thinking.description: Switches between thinking and non-thinking modes. Not required.

thinking_budget.description: Maximum number of tokens for chain-of-thought output. Not required.

prompt_cache.description: Anthropic prompt caching (cache_control breakpoints on tools, system and the latest messages). "5m"/"1h" = cache TTL (1h costs 2x on writes), "off" = disabled. Unset: uses customcopilot.promptCacheTtl for Claude and MiniMax-M2 models, off for other Anthropic-compatible models. Only affects apiMode anthropic/zai.

image_max_dimension.description: Long-edge pixel cap for images sent to this model (0 = never resize). Overrides customcopilot.imageMaxDimension.

fast_mode.description: Anthropic fast mode: sends speed "fast" (up to 2.5x output tokens/s at premium pricing). Claude Opus 5.5 (GA), Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 (research preview, beta header added automatically). A fast-mode 429/529 falls back to standard speed. Only affects apiMode anthropic.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature (range: [0, 2]). Lower values make output more deterministic, higher values make it more creative. Default is 0.

top_k.description: Top-k sampling value (range: [1, Infinity)). Not required.

effort.description: Reasoning effort level for OpenRouter/xAI (high, medium, low, minimal, auto)

exclude.description: Exclude reasoning tokens from the final response

max_tokens.description: Specific token limit for reasoning (Anthropic-style, alternative to effort)

enabled.description: Enable reasoning (inferred from effort or max_tokens if not specified)

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to be sent with every request to this model's provider. These headers will be merged with the default headers (Authorization, Content-Type, User-Agent).

include_reasoning_in_request.description: Whether to include reasoning_content in assistant messages sent to the API. Support deepseek-v3.2 or others.

apiMode.description: API mode: 'openai' (Default) for OpenAI Chat Completions (/chat/completions), 'openai-responses' for OpenAI Responses (/responses), 'ollama' for Ollama (/api/chat), 'anthropic' for Anthropic (/v1/messages), 'gemini' for Gemini (*/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse), 'zai' for Z.AI free tier (Anthropic-compatible with Bearer auth at https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic).

useForCommitGeneration.description: Whether this model is used for Git commit message generation. Supported for all apiModes.

delay.description: Model-specific delay in milliseconds between consecutive requests. If not specified, falls back to global customcopilot.delay configuration.

customcopilot.models.description: A list of preferred models to use. If provided, these models will be used directly instead of fetching from the API.

enabled.description: Enable retry mechanism for api errors. Default is true.

max_attempts.description: Maximum number of retry attempts. Default is 3.

interval_ms.description: Interval between retry attempts in milliseconds. Default is 1000 (1 seconds).

status_codes.description: Additional HTTP status codes that will be merged. Default is [429, 500, 502, 503, 504].

customcopilot.retry.description: Retry configuration for handling api errors like [429, 500, 502, 503, 504].

customcopilot.chatRetries.markdownDescription: Automatic chat-level retries ("auto Try Again"). When a chat request fails **before any content has been streamed**, the whole generation is re-run transparently so you don't have to press *Try Again*. `0` disables it (default), `-1` retries forever, and any positive number is the maximum extra attempts. Already-streamed output is never duplicated. Applies to all API modes.

customcopilot.chatRetryInterval.description: Delay in milliseconds between automatic chat-level retries (customcopilot.chatRetries). Default is 1000 (1 second).

customcopilot.chatRetryJitter.markdownDescription: Optional random extra delay (in milliseconds) added on top of `customcopilot.chatRetryInterval` before each automatic chat retry. A random value between `0` and this number is picked for every retry, spreading retries out so a batch of chats that failed together don't all hit the endpoint at the same time. `0` disables jitter (default).

customcopilot.delay.description: Fixed delay in milliseconds between consecutive requests. Default is 0 (no delay).

customcopilot.subagent.model.markdownDescription: Fallback model for `#delegate` subagents when the main chat's model is unavailable and no `model` hint is given. By default subagents run on **the exact model selected in the chat** (the same config, even when several configs share one model id); sub-agents inherit their parent's model. An id or name substring (e.g. `glm-4.7-flash`).

customcopilot.subagent.maxSteps.markdownDescription: Default maximum tool-calling rounds for a `#delegate` subagent before it must write its report (cap 60).

customcopilot.subagent.maxConcurrent.markdownDescription: Maximum number of subagents (all nesting levels) running at the same time.

customcopilot.subagent.maxStartsPerTurn.markdownDescription: Maximum number of agents the main chat may start within one turn (one user message and its tool rounds). Protects against a model that keeps spawning agents in a loop.

customcopilot.subagent.maxDepth.markdownDescription: How deep subagents may nest: `1` = only the main chat starts agents; `3` (default) = agents can start sub-agents, which can start their own. Sub-agents inherit their parent's model; their reports go to the parent.

customcopilot.subagent.compactThreshold.markdownDescription: Auto-compact a subagent's context when it reaches this share of the model's input window (`0.8` = 80%): the same model summarizes the work so far and the history is replaced by the task + summary. A context-overflow error also triggers one compaction and a retry.

enumDescriptions: Ask, except when the main chat runs in Autopilot or VS Code's global tool auto-approve (`chat.tools.global.autoApprove`) is on.
Never ask — agents run shell commands without confirmation.
customcopilot.subagent.autoApproveComman.markdownDescription: Whether shell commands of write-enabled background agents need your approval. The approval is a non-modal notification; the agent waits until you answer.

customcopilot.subagent.commandsInTermina.markdownDescription: Run agents' shell commands in a visible VS Code terminal per agent ("Agent a7 …", via shell integration) so you can watch them. Falls back to a hidden process when shell integration is unavailable.

customcopilot.subagent.autoResume.markdownDescription: When a background agent finishes (or messages the main agent) after the main chat turn has ended, post its report as a new message to **the chat session that started it**, so the main agent continues working. When the main agent is blocked in `waitForAgents` it is woken directly instead. After 3 consecutive turns started by such posts (no user message in between), newly started agents no longer auto-post (their reports stay readable via `wait`), so agents → report → agents loops cannot run forever. If you pressed **Stop** in the chat, reports are not posted automatically (VS Code would ask about your queued messages) — a notification offers to post them instead.

customcopilot.recommendedPrompt.markdownDescription: **Recommended.** Add the extension's recommended prompt to the system prompt Copilot assembles for your models in agent mode (requests with tools): Claude Code–style working rules (read before editing, minimal changes, care with destructive actions, dedicated tools over shell, parallel tool calls, concise answers) and — when the delegate tool is available — the background-agents guide (agent types, every agent action with examples, how to brief an agent, the start → end turn → report flow, never invent agent results). Model-agnostic; applied after `#customcopilot.promptOverride.enabled#`. Titles and summaries are untouched. Preview it in the configuration view → Global Settings → System prompt.

customcopilot.subagent.worktreeDir.markdownDescription: Where `isolation: "worktree"` agents get their git worktrees: a folder relative to the repository root (added to `.git/info/exclude`, never to a tracked file), or an absolute folder (a sub-folder per repository). Worktrees are named `agent-<id>-<rand>` on branch `worktree-agent-<id>-<rand>`. Unchanged ones are removed when the agent finishes (and at startup); changed ones are kept until you apply or remove them from the agent's details.

customcopilot.subagent.worktreeSymlinks.markdownDescription: Folders (relative to the repository root) to symlink from the main checkout into every agent worktree instead of leaving them missing — e.g. `node_modules`, `.venv`. Git-ignored files listed in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the repository root (e.g. `.env`) are copied in.

customcopilot.subagent.pauseChat.markdownDescription: Pause the main chat while the background agents it started are working: in the turn that started them, calls that only wait for / poll the agents (`wait`/`status`, `sleep` commands, todo updates) are not executed — the turn ends with a *Chat paused* note instead, and every agent report is posted into the chat as a new message that continues the work. Real work and starting more agents still go through. Needs `#customcopilot.subagent.autoResume#`. Disable to let the main agent block in `wait`.

customcopilot.subagent.autoResumeIdleMs.markdownDescription: How long (ms) the main chat must be idle (no model request or agent tool call) before an agent report is auto-posted to it.

customcopilot.schedule.enabled.markdownDescription: Fire scheduled wake-ups / reminders (`#schedule`). When off, due wake-ups wait (they are not lost) until it is turned on again.

customcopilot.schedule.minDelaySeconds.markdownDescription: Earliest wake-up (and shortest repeat interval) the chat agent may schedule, in seconds. Reminders you create yourself may be sooner.

customcopilot.schedule.maxPending.markdownDescription: How many wake-ups the chat agent may have pending at once.

customcopilot.schedule.maxChain.markdownDescription: Loop guard: the chat agent may not schedule new wake-ups after this many consecutive automatic turns (wake-ups / agent reports) without a message from you. Recurring wake-ups you approved keep running.

customcopilot.imageMaxDimension.markdownDescription: Images (attachments, screenshots, tool results) whose long edge exceeds this many pixels are downscaled and re-encoded as JPEG before being sent, so a 4K screenshot does not eat the context window (GLM vision bills raw pixels). Use `1024`–`1568` for maximum savings, `0` to send images unchanged. Per-model `image_max_dimension` overrides this.

enumDescriptions: 5-minute cache (writes 1.25x input price, refreshed free on every hit).
1-hour cache (writes 2x input price) — better when you often pause longer than 5 minutes.
customcopilot.promptCacheTtl.markdownDescription: Default Anthropic prompt-cache TTL for Claude (and MiniMax-M2) models on `apiMode` `anthropic`/`zai`. The extension places `cache_control` breakpoints on the tool list, the system prompt and the latest messages (max 4) so agent loops reuse the cached prefix (cache reads cost ~10% of input). Per-model `prompt_cache` overrides this.

customcopilot.commitLanguage.description: Language for generated Git commit messages. Default is English.

customcopilot.commitMessagePrompt.description: Custom system prompt for commit message generation. If not provided, uses the default prompt.

customcopilot.readFileLines.description: Number of lines to read when using `read_file` tool. Large lines may cost more tokens. Default is 0, let model decide lines.

customcopilot.userAgent.default: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/147.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
customcopilot.userAgent.description: Custom User-Agent string to use for API requests. Default is a Chrome-based User-Agent.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_delegateTask
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Start and manage SUBAGENTS — independent agent loops on the same model as this chat, each in a FRESH context (they cannot see this conversation), with this chat's workspace tools, their own terminal and (allowWrite / worktree) their own edit tools; each returns ONE final report.

`action` selects the operation (this one tool does everything). Shortcut: {"task": "wait"} or {"task": "status"} without `action` work too:
- "start" (default): start an agent. Requires `task` (self-contained briefing: goal and why, exact paths/symbols, what is known or ruled out, constraints, whether to write code or only research), `name` (3-7 word title) and `expectedOutput` (report format/length). Optional `subagentType` (general-purpose | Explore | Plan | custom — see action "types") and `isolation: "worktree"` (own git working copy; edits never touch the user's files). Runs in the BACKGROUND and returns immediately with the agent id; launch independent agents in the same response so they run in parallel.
- "wait": return pending reports. While the chat is paused for its agents (the default) it does NOT block — end your turn instead; for agents that do not post to the chat it BLOCKS until one finishes or messages you. Never poll with no-op commands or placeholder agents.
- "status": list agents as a tree (type, status, activity, context, rounds, worktree); with `id` the full details and report of one agent.
- "message": send `message` to the running agent `id` (read at its next round) — steer it, answer its question.
- "stop": stop agent `id` (or "all") with its sub-agents.
- "resume": continue a finished/stopped agent `id` with a follow-up `message`; it keeps its full previous context (and worktree).
- "types": list the agent types with their descriptions.

WHEN TO START AGENTS: substantial, self-contained work that would flood your context or can run in parallel — broad codebase exploration (Explore), implementation planning (Plan), multi-file research, reviews, independent implementation chunks (allowWrite, ideally isolation "worktree").
NEVER start an agent for: trivial work (one read/search/answer — do it yourself), tests or demos of this tool, placeholders, acknowledging or reacting to an agent report, waiting (use action "wait"), work needing the user's input, or work an agent already does (check action "status"). Never delegate understanding ("based on your findings, fix it") — include paths, lines and what to change.

WHILE AGENTS RUN the chat PAUSES: start all agents you need, then END YOUR TURN with a short status message to the user — waiting, polling, sleep and todo updates are not executed in that turn. Never predict or invent an agent's results. Each report is posted into this chat as a message when its agent finishes and you continue the user's task then (this is the normal flow). Limits: customcopilot.subagent.maxConcurrent running, maxStartsPerTurn per turn.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a self-contained sub-task in a background agent on the same model; its report comes back when it finishes.

action.description: Operation (default "start"). "types" lists the available agent types (subagentType).

subagentType.description: Agent type: "general-purpose" (default; research and multi-step work, edits with allowWrite), "Explore" (fast read-only codebase search — say "quick", "medium" or "very thorough" in the task), "Plan" (read-only architect: step-by-step plan + critical files), or a custom agent from .claude/agents / .github/agents (action "types" lists them).

isolation.description: "worktree": run the agent in its own git worktree (separate working copy on its own branch) — its edits never touch the user's files; write tools are enabled there. An unchanged worktree is removed automatically; otherwise path, branch and change summary come with the report.

task.description: Self-contained task: the goal, exact paths/symbols, constraints, what is already known and what must NOT be done. The agent cannot see this conversation.

name.description: Short descriptive title of the sub-task, 3-7 words (e.g. 'Map auth token refresh flow'). Shown in the agent map and used to address the agent.

expectedOutput.description: Exact content/format of the final report (e.g. 'bullet list of file:line with a one-line explanation each', 'unified diff summary', 'yes/no + evidence').

id.description: Agent id or name (for status details, message, stop, resume; "all" for stop).

ids.description: Agents to wait for (action "wait"); default: any.

message.description: Text for action "message" or the follow-up instruction for "resume".

timeoutSeconds.description: Max wait for action "wait" (default 600, max 3600; 0 = only read pending reports).

background.description: Default true: run in the background and return immediately. false: wait here for the report.

model.description: Optional model override: an id/name substring (e.g. 'glm-4.7-flash') or 'fast'. Default: the same model as this chat.

allowWrite.description: Give the subagent tools that modify the workspace (edits/terminal). Default false (read-only).

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_listAgents
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the background agents as a tree (who started whom): id, name, status (running/done/failed/stopped), current activity, context usage (tokens / window), rounds used, unread messages. With `id` (agent id or name) returns that agent's full details: task, status, error, its sub-agents and its full report. Use it before starting a new agent (avoid duplicates), to check progress, or to read a report again. It never waits — to wait for completion use customcopilot_waitForAgents.

id.description: Optional agent id or name for full details and report.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_sendAgentMessage
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Send a message to a RUNNING background agent: by id or name, or to every running agent with to: "all". The recipient reads it at the start of its next round (it is not interrupted mid-tool). Use it to steer an agent (new information, changed requirements, narrower scope), answer a question an agent asked you, or tell it to wrap up. Subagents use to: "main" to message the main agent, or another agent's id to coordinate. Finished agents cannot receive messages — use customcopilot_resumeAgent to continue one.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Send a message to a background agent.

to.description: Agent id or name, "all", or "main" (subagents only).

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_waitForAgents
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Block until a background agent finishes or sends you a message, then return ALL pending agent reports/messages for this chat plus the agent list. Wakes up immediately when something arrives. Use it when you have nothing else useful to do while agents run, instead of polling customcopilot_listAgents. `ids`: wait until all of these agents have finished (a message also wakes you). `timeoutSeconds`: maximum wait (default 600, max 3600); 0 = only read pending notifications without waiting. After it returns, continue the user's task with the reports — do not start new agents merely to confirm them. If you have nothing else to do while agents run, you may instead simply end your turn: reports are posted into the chat automatically.

ids.description: Optional agent ids/names to wait for (all must finish).

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_stopAgent
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Stop a running background agent (by id or name) together with all its sub-agents, or every agent with id "all". Use it when an agent is no longer needed, went off track, or duplicates other work. A stopped agent keeps its conversation and can be continued with customcopilot_resumeAgent.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_resumeAgent
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Continue a finished, stopped or failed background agent with a new instruction. It resumes from its FULL previous conversation (no need to repeat context), gets a fresh step budget and reports again when done — cheaper and better than starting a new agent for follow-up work on the same topic. `message`: the follow-up instruction. `background` (default true): false waits here for the new report. For a RUNNING agent use customcopilot_sendAgentMessage instead. Subagents can resume only their own sub-agents.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Continue a finished background agent with its previous context.

background.description: Default true. false: wait here for the new report.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_searchSkills
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search global agent-skill catalogs (skills.sh, hermes-agent repo) for installable SKILL.md skills. ALWAYS search with ENGLISH keywords (the catalogs are English-indexed; translate the user's request first). Results are ranked by trust (first-party owners like anthropics/openai/github, install counts) and include the FULL SKILL.md of the top candidates: read them, analyze which one actually fits the user's need, then call installSkill with the exact name.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the skills.sh / hermes-agent catalogs for installable skills.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_installSkill
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Install a skill from the catalog into ~/.copilot/skills (available to Copilot Chat immediately). Calls searchSkills first if needed; pick a TRUSTED result (first-party owner or high installs) that matches the need. Always asks the user for confirmation. If the skill validates as CRITICAL, installation is refused and you receive a manual-review package: show ALL critical aspects to the user verbatim, offer a risk analysis with the current model, and never retry the install until the issues are fixed.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Install a skill from the catalog (with confirmation).

query.description: The search query that found the skill (used to re-resolve it).

name.description: Exact skill name from searchSkills results.

source.description: Catalog the skill was found in. Default: skills.sh.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_readSkill
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the full SKILL.md (frontmatter + body) of an installed skill. Use before improving a skill, or when the user asks what an installed skill does. Also lists installed skills when the name is not found.

name.description: Skill name (as shown in the installed list).

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_improveSkill
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Rewrite an INSTALLED skill in place with an improved SKILL.md body (self-improvement). First readSkill to see the current content, then send the FULL new body. Requires a short summary of what changed (shown to the user in the confirmation). Always asks the user to confirm; refuses critical content (dangerous shell patterns). Use when the user says a skill behaved poorly, is outdated, or should be refined.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what changed and why.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_createSkill
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a NEW skill from scratch in ~/.copilot/skills when nothing suitable exists in the catalogs (searchSkills first!). Write a focused SKILL.md body (markdown instructions; name in frontmatter is derived from the name field). Always asks the user to confirm. Use when the user wants to capture a reusable workflow as a skill.

name.description: Skill name: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens.

description.description: What the skill does; Copilot uses this to decide when to load it.

languageModelTools.name: customcopilot_scheduleWakeup
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Schedule a WAKE-UP: the `prompt` is posted into THIS chat later as a new message (once the chat is idle) and you continue from it — Claude Code ScheduleWakeup/cron style. Survives a window reload.

- Once: {"prompt": "<what to do then — self-contained>", "reason": "<short label>", "delaySeconds": 900} or {"at": "14:30"} (or an ISO date-time).
- Recurring: add "everySeconds" (≥ 60) and optionally "maxRuns".
- {"action": "list"} — pending wake-ups; {"action": "cancel", "id": "w3"} — cancel one.

USE IT for state that changes outside this chat (CI runs, deploys, long builds, external queues — choose a delay matched to how fast it changes: one check after ~8 min for an 8-minute CI run, not many short polls), for follow-ups the user asked for ("remind me…", "check again in an hour", "every morning…"), and for loops the user explicitly requested.
NEVER use it to wait for background agents (their reports arrive automatically) or for short polling. After scheduling, END YOUR TURN with a one-line status. A message starting with "⏰ Scheduled wake-up" is such a wake-up, not a user message: do what its prompt says; schedule the next one only if still needed, and cancel recurring ones you no longer need.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Post a prompt into this chat later (once or repeatedly) — reminders, CI checks, follow-ups.

prompt.description: Message posted into the chat when it fires — self-contained: what to check or do and why.

reason.description: Short label shown in the schedule (e.g. 'Check CI run #812').

at.description: Fire at a time: "HH:MM" (today, or tomorrow if past) or an ISO date-time.

everySeconds.description: Repeat interval in seconds (≥ 60). Without delaySeconds/at the first run is one interval from now.

maxRuns.description: Recurring: stop after this many runs.
